title: Hausdorff-null sets with a uniform small-ball mass bound are μ-null
statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on ℝ^N = Euclidean N (Borel σ-algebra), let A ⊆ ℝ^N be an arbitrary set, let c ∈ [0, ∞) and δ > 0. Suppose H^n(A) = 0, where H^n = μHE[n], and suppose μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ c · ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)^n for every x ∈ A and every real ρ with 0 < ρ ≤ δ, where B_ρ(x) is the closed ball. Then μ(A) = 0. Here μ(A) is the outer measure of A; A need not be measurable.
lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (A : Set (Euclidean N)) (c : ℝ≥0∞) (δ : ℝ), c ≠ ∞ → 0 < δ → μHE[n] A = 0 → (∀ x ∈ A, ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ρ ≤ δ → μ (closedBall x ρ) ≤ c * ENNReal.ofReal ρ ^ n) → μ A = 0
